name: Battle of Pydna

phases.title: The armies stand drawn up
phases.text: The Romans put their two legions in the middle with allied infantry on the flanks and cavalry on the wings. The Macedonian phalanx held the centre, with the Guard on its left, light troops on both flanks and Perseus with the cavalry on the right.

phases.title: The two centres engage
phases.text: The Macedonians advanced on the Romans a short distance from the Roman camp. The Roman allies tried to beat down the pikes or hack off their points, but with little success.

phases.title: The allies retreat and the phalanx loses its line
phases.text: Unable to get under the thick bristle of pikes, the Romans used a planned retreat over the rough ground. As the phalanx pushed on into the foothills the ground became uneven and its line lost cohesion.

phases.title: Paullus sends the legions into the gaps
phases.text: Paullus ordered the legions into the gaps and they attacked the phalangites on their exposed flanks. At close quarters the longer Roman sword and heavier shield prevailed over the lighter Macedonian arms.

phases.title: The Roman right routs the Macedonian left
phases.text: The Roman right succeeded in routing the Macedonian left, and it then joined the legions, who were already fighting the phalangites on their exposed flanks.

phases.title: Perseus flees with the right-wing cavalry
phases.text: Seeing the tide of battle turn, Perseus fled with the cavalry on the Macedonian right, leaving the infantry still fighting on the field.

phases.title: The Guard fights to the death
phases.text: The 3,000-strong Guard fought to the death. Nearly 11,000 Macedonians were captured, and the pursuit lasted until nightfall, though the battle itself lasted about an hour.

note: The accounts do not give the compass directions, so none is drawn. The foothills of Mount Olocrus are placed on the Roman side of the field; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. The Roman camp is placed in them. Other accounts say the Macedonian cavalry did not fight, or that a corps of 10,000 Macedonians was cut off; the plan follows the main account. The accounts do not say where the Macedonian left-wing cavalry stood or how the Roman allies were divided between the wings.
